result.title: RAMP: Rethinking Multimodal Evaluation through Answer Readout Protocols
result.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are often evaluated by converting model outputs into discrete answers. The conversion protocol determines which scores become predictions and can strongly influence the reported results. We introduce RAMP (Readout Aware Multimodal Protocol), a systematic framework that compares direct yes/no token logits, surface-form scores, and typed or reversed A/B interfaces under fixed model checkpoints and paired visual questions. On 500 POPE adversarial questions, typed versus bare readout changes accuracy by $-20.2$ percentage points for SmolVLM-256M, $-16.4$ for TinyLLaVA-1.1B, and $+1.8$ for Qwen2.5-VL-3B. Paired transitions reveal extensive prediction changes even when the net accuracy difference is small: 79 of 104 binary ChartQA items change correctness for SmolVLM-500M, despite a $+1.0$-point net difference. We further analyze prompt wording, candidate forms, option position, cross-task effects, and calibration. An independent offline replay reproduces 16,140 first-token decisions from saved raw scores with exact agreement. Our findings establish answer readout as a measurable component of multimodal evaluation and provide a reproducible protocol for analyzing model comparisons.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 RAMP 框架，在固定模型与配对视觉问题上系统比较 yes/no logit、表面形式分数和 typed/reversed A/B 等答案读出协议，并用 POPE、ChartQA 等展示读出方式可让准确率变动数十个百分点、且逐题预测大量翻转。
AI.relevance_reason: 这是多模态评价侧的诊断工作：它说明读出协议本身就能左右得分，可供核查 LVR 与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 类方法在准确率比较中是否被答案解析差异混淆，尤其涉及配对翻转与校准分析。
